types.name: ProductCustomization
types.description:
A choice the merchant lets the buyer make about a product — an engraving, a
gift wrap, a cut to size, an uploaded file.

Distinct from a variant option: this does not select a variant, it rides along
with the line, usually changes its price, and is part of what makes one line
different from another.

fields.name: id
fields.description: A globally-unique identifier. Send it back as `CartLineInput.customizations[].customizationId`.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
How the buyer answers:

`select`, `radio`, `checkbox` — one of `values`, sent as its id
`text`, `textarea` — free text
`weight`, `length` — a number, in the unit named by `valueSymbol`
`square` — two numbers, length and width, sent as `values`
`file` — a file the buyer uploads with `cartCustomizationFileUpload`; the
handle it returns is the answer. `fileUpload` gives the limits.

fields.name: label
fields.description: The label shown to the buyer.

fields.name: required
fields.description: Whether the merchant marked it as required.

fields.name: multiple
fields.description: Whether the buyer may choose more than one of `values`.

fields.name: sortOrder
fields.description: The display order among a product's customizations.

fields.name: price
fields.description:
A fixed sum this adds to the line, when the charge is on the customization
itself rather than on the value chosen. Null when the values carry the
charge, when it is free, or when the merchant charges a percentage — see
`percentage`.

fields.name: percentage
fields.description:
A share of the product's price this adds, as a percentage — `10.00` means
ten percent. Set instead of `price` when the merchant charges
proportionally. Null otherwise.

fields.name: perItem
fields.description: Whether the charge applies once for the line or per unit bought.

fields.name: valueSymbol
fields.description: The unit the buyer enters, for the measured types — `cm`, `kg`, and so on.

types.name: MobileAppConfig
types.description:
The merchant's design for this store's native mobile app — colours, typography,
home-screen layout, bottom tabs and feature flags.

Read it once at boot and drive the shell from it. It changes only when the merchant
saves in their admin panel, so a client is expected to cache it and re-render when
`version` moves.

**Every field is nullable, and null means "the merchant has no opinion — use your own
default".** It does not mean "empty". An unconfigured store answers with nulls
throughout, and a client that treats those as values would paint the platform's
placeholder colours over the branding it was built with.

Deliberately permissive on the wire. There are no enums here and `MobileAppSection` is
a flat record with a `type` string rather than a union, because a client that ships a
fragment or an enum case the server does not have yet fails the WHOLE query and gets no
config at all — the opposite of graceful. An unknown string costs one ignored section.

fields.name: schema
fields.description:
The shape's version. Bumped when a change cannot be absorbed by a client holding an
older cached copy; such a client should discard its cache rather than migrate it.

fields.name: version
fields.description:
A stamp over the config's contents. Unchanged means nothing was saved since the last
read, so a client can skip its re-render and its cache write.

fields.name: colors
fields.description: Palette. Null members keep the client's compiled colour.

fields.name: typography
fields.description: Type family and the density scale.

fields.name: home
fields.description: The home screen's composition.

fields.name: tabs
fields.description:
The bottom tabs, in the order they should render. Null when the merchant has never
configured them. A tab absent from this list is not part of the app; a tab present
with `enabled: false` was deliberately switched off.

fields.name: features
fields.description: Which optional features the merchant wants surfaced.

fields.name: catalog
fields.description: How the catalogue grid is laid out.

fields.name: product
fields.description: What the product page shows around the gallery.

fields.name: branding
fields.description: Images the app shows as the store's identity.

fields.name: style
fields.description: Shape. What the app's own look is made of, beyond colour and type.

fields.name: pages
fields.description:
The app's own landing pages, in the merchant's order: only their ids and titles. Read a page's
sections with `mobileAppPage(id:)` when it is opened. A link or tab of type `appPage` names one of
these by id; the server drops links and tabs to a page that no longer exists.

fields.name: menu
fields.description:
The merchant's menu: a list of links, opened by the ☰ button on the home screen (when `showOnHome`) and by
a tab of type `menu`. Links only, no icons.

fields.name: reviews
fields.description:
How the Product reviews app shows ratings, read from that app's own settings — the switches the web
storefront's product lists and product page follow. Null when the app is not installed or is off.

fields.name: labels
fields.description:
The product ribbons' colours from the web theme's Labels settings (Design → Labels), so the app paints
New, Featured, Sale and the discount badge as the web store does. A member or colour the theme does not
set is null, and the app keeps its own. The merchant's own product labels carry their colours on
`Product.labels` and are not affected.

types.name: MobileAppLabels
types.description: The theme's ribbon colours, per kind of ribbon.

fields.name: new
fields.description: The New ribbon. `name` is its text, as `Product.labels` gives it, so the client can tell it apart.

fields.name: featured
fields.description: The Featured ribbon. `name` as for `new`.

fields.name: sale
fields.description: The Sale ribbon, on a product whose price fell with no discount to quote.

fields.name: discount
fields.description: The discount badge (`-15%`).

types.name: MobileAppLabelStyle
types.description: One ribbon's text and colours. Colours are `#rrggbb`.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The ribbon's text as `Product.labels` gives it, for the platform's New and Featured; null for the Sale ribbon and the discount badge.

fields.name: background
fields.description: The ribbon's background colour; null when the theme does not set it as a plain colour.

fields.name: text
fields.description: The ribbon's text colour; null when the theme does not set it as a plain colour.

types.name: MobileAppReviews
types.description: The Product reviews app's display settings (Apps → Product reviews), as the web storefront applies them.

fields.name: showInListing
fields.description: The star rating under the name on product cards in lists (`show_in_listing`).

fields.name: hideEmptyRating
fields.description: A product with no rating yet shows no stars at all, rather than five empty ones (`hidden_rating`).

types.name: MobileAppMenu
types.description: The merchant's menu of links for the app.

fields.name: showOnHome
fields.description: Whether the home screen shows the menu (see `homeStyle`). Nothing to show while `items` is empty.

fields.name: homeStyle
fields.description:
How the home screen shows it while `showOnHome`: `button` — the ☰ in the top bar opens a drawer; `bar` — the
links themselves in a row under the top bar. Treat a value you do not know as `button`.

fields.name: items
fields.description: The links, in the merchant's order.

types.name: MobileAppMenuItem
types.description:
One link of the menu. `type` is what a tab the merchant adds can open: `appPage`, `page`, `category`,
`collection`, `product` or `url`, with `value` as for a tab. Skip a type you do not know.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Identifies the link within the menu, where it is unique.

fields.name: type
fields.description: What the link opens: `appPage`, `page`, `category`, `collection`, `product` or `url`.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The target, as a tab's `value`: a page handle, an id or a web address.

fields.name: label
fields.description: The link's text. Null only when the target had no name to take.

types.name: MobileAppPageRef
types.description: One of the app's landing pages, as the config lists it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable across renames — what links and tabs point at.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The page's name, for a screen header.

types.name: MobileAppPage
types.description:
One of the app's landing pages: a screen built from the same sections as the home screen. Render its
sections exactly as the home screen's.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable across renames — what links and tabs point at.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The page's name, for the screen header.

fields.name: version
fields.description: A stamp over the page's contents. Unchanged means nothing was saved since the last read.

fields.name: sections
fields.description: The sections to render, top to bottom. May be empty.

types.name: MobileAppStyle
types.description:
The store's shape language.

Separate from `colors` and `typography` because it is neither: these are the decisions that make
two stores with the same palette still look like different shops.

fields.name: buttonRadius
fields.description:
How round every button in the app is: `sharp`, `soft`, `rounded` or `pill`.

One value for all of them — the app had a rounded primary button and pill call-to-actions on
the home screen, which read as two different apps stitched together. A name rather than a
number: the client owns the pixels, so a later release can retune a step without a config
migration, and a value it does not recognise falls back to its own default.

Null when the merchant has never chosen — keep the client's compiled default.

types.name: MobileAppBranding
types.description: The store's identity inside the app.

fields.name: logoUrl
fields.description:
The logo on the Home tab of the bottom bar. Null means the merchant has not uploaded one for
the app — keep the tab's house icon. (Clients before this rule fell back to `shop.logoUrl`.)

types.name: MobileAppColors
types.description:
The app's palette, as six-digit hex (`#rrggbb`).

Null on any member means the client keeps whatever it compiled in.

fields.name: brand
fields.description: Primary brand colour — tab bar accent, buttons, hero.

fields.name: onBrand
fields.description:
Foreground on top of `brand`.

Null does NOT mean black: it means derive one, which for this app is a relative
luminance test against the brand colour. A merchant only sets this to overrule a
bad automatic pick.

fields.name: ink
fields.description: Primary text colour.

fields.name: surface
fields.description: Recessed background behind cards and thumbnails.

fields.name: border
fields.description: Hairline and divider colour.

fields.name: sale
fields.description: Sale / discounted price colour.

fields.name: success
fields.description: Success and in-stock colour.

fields.name: background
fields.description: Background behind every screen (home, listings, product page, cart, account). `surface` panels sit on top of it.

types.name: MobileAppTypography
types.description: Type family and density.

fields.name: family
fields.description:
The family's display name, e.g. `Inter`. `System` means the platform's own font —
render it and download nothing.

fields.name: scale
fields.description:
Multiplier on the app's root type size. Also scales the spacing ramp derived from
it, so it reads as a density control rather than a font-size control.

fields.name: files
fields.description: Where to download each weight from. Null for `System`.

fields.name: headingFamily
fields.description:
A second family for headings: section titles, screen titles, the product name, a
banner's title. Null means headings use `family`. `System` means the platform's own font.

fields.name: headingFiles
fields.description: Where to download the heading family's weights from. Null when `headingFamily` is null or `System`.

types.name: MobileAppFontFiles
types.description:
One downloadable font file per weight, because a font registered at runtime cannot have
its weight synthesised — a single file registered under one name renders at that one
weight whatever weight is asked for.

Any member may be null when the family has no cut at that weight. Fall back rather than
skipping the family: medium ← regular, semiBold ← bold ← regular. With no `regular`
there is nothing to fall back from, so use the system font.

fields.name: regular
fields.description: Weight 400.

fields.name: medium
fields.description: Weight 500.

fields.name: semiBold
fields.description: Weight 600.

fields.name: bold
fields.description: Weight 700.

types.name: MobileAppHome
types.description: The home screen's composition.

fields.name: sections
fields.description:
The sections to render, top to bottom. Null when the merchant has never configured
the home screen. Render each section independently — one that fails to load its
data should render nothing and leave the rest of the screen standing.

types.name: MobileAppSection
types.description:
One home-screen section.

A flat record covering every section type: fields that do not apply to this section's
`type` are null. Switch on `type` and ignore a section whose type you do not recognise —
that is the intended forward-compatibility path, and the reason this is not a union.

fields.name: id
fields.description:
Stable per-instance identity, unique within the list.

Not the type: a merchant may legitimately place two of the same type — two banner strips for
two campaigns, two product rails for two collections — and a client that keys its rendering on
the type collapses them into one. Use this as the render key.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
What to render: `banner`, `categories`, `products`, `bannerList`, `countdown`, `html`, `video`,
`recentlyViewed`, `brands`, `featuredProduct` or `bannerProduct` — or, for a schema-1 client, `hero` and `banners` instead of `banner`. Treat any other value as a section to skip; more types will be added without
a schema version bump, and skipping is what lets the store serve one before this client knows it.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: False when the merchant kept the section but switched it off.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Heading. Null means use the app's own translated heading for this section type.

fields.name: eyebrow
fields.description:
`hero` only. The small line ABOVE the heading — the eyebrow. Null means use the app's own
translated one (`sfapp.home.hero.title`), which is what a merchant who never touched it gets.

fields.name: subtitle
fields.description: `hero` only. Supporting line under the heading.

fields.name: ctaLabel
fields.description:
`hero`, `countdown` and `bannerList`. Text ON THE BUTTON, and nothing else: null means no button
is rendered at all, not that the app should substitute a heading for it. On a `hero` the card
itself stays tappable either way — see `linkType`. On a `bannerList` the button sits UNDER the
tiles: it is the "see all" beneath a row of category banners, where each tile opens one category
and the button opens the lot.

fields.name: imageUrl
fields.description:
`hero` only. Background image. Render a scrim over it regardless of the image —
a merchant will eventually upload a light photo behind light text.

fields.name: linkType
fields.description:
`hero` and `bannerList`. What the call-to-action opens: `none`, `catalog`, `category`,
`product`, `url` or `appPage`. Unknown values should behave as `none`.

fields.name: linkValue
fields.description: `hero` and `bannerList`. The target for `linkType` — a category id, product id, absolute URL, or an app page id (`appPage`, see `MobileAppConfig.pages`).

fields.name: height
fields.description:
`hero` only. Height in points. Null means as tall as its own copy, which is what every hero
was before the field existed. A value is a MINIMUM, not a cap: copy that does not fit still
grows the banner rather than being clipped.

fields.name: contentAlign
fields.description:
`hero` only. Where the block of copy sits vertically: `top`, `middle` or `bottom`. Null and
unknown values mean `middle`. Only visible on a hero given a `height` taller than its copy.

fields.name: textAlign
fields.description:
`hero` only. How the copy and the button are aligned: `left`, `center` or `right`. Null and
unknown values mean `left`.

fields.name: overlay
fields.description:
`hero` only. How dark the scrim over the background image is, in percent. Null means 35.
Clamp it into 20–70 before use: the copy is drawn light whatever the merchant chose, so a
scrim that can reach zero is a hero that can become unreadable over a pale photograph.
Ignored by a hero with no image.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: `categories`, `products` and `recentlyViewed`. How many items to fetch. Clamp it before use.

fields.name: layout
fields.description:
`products` and `brands`. How the cards are arranged: `grid` (the wrapping grid of `columns` per row)
or `carousel` (one row that slides sideways). Unknown or absent values should render the grid.

fields.name: columns
fields.description:
`products`, `recentlyViewed`, `brands` and `bannerList`. Grid columns — 2 or 3 for products,
2 to 4 for brands, 1 to 3 for a banner list, where 1 is the stacked full-width list. Clamp it
before use. Ignored by a `carousel`.

fields.name: categoryItems
fields.description:
`categories` only. The merchant's hand-picked shortcuts, in order. Empty means the automatic
strip — the first `limit` categories — which is what every store saved before this field renders.
Skip a shortcut whose category no longer resolves.

fields.name: display
fields.description:
`categories` only. What a shortcut shows: `both` (picture and name), `text` or `image`. Null and
unknown values mean `both`. Schema 2.

fields.name: imageShape
fields.description:
`categories` only. The shape a shortcut's picture is cut to: `circle`, `rounded` or `square`.
Null and unknown values mean `circle`. Schema 2.

fields.name: vendorIds
fields.description: `brands` only. Vendor ids, in order; resolve them with the `vendors` query. Empty renders nothing.

fields.name: collectionId
fields.description:
`products` only. Which collection to draw from. Null means the store's featured set.
Superseded by `productSource` and `sourceIds` where those are served: a store keeps writing the
first picked category here (and null for any other source), so a client that predates them still
shows something sensible.

fields.name: productSource
fields.description:
`products` only. Where the products come from, as the web storefront's Product showcase picks
them: `all`, `category`, `collection` (a smart collection), `vendor`, `product` (hand-picked) or
`tag`. Null means `all` — or, with a `collectionId`, that one category. Unknown values mean `all`.

fields.name: sourceIds
fields.description:
`products` only. The values for `productSource`, in the merchant's order: category, smart
collection, vendor or product ids — or, for `tag`, the tags' text. Several values of one source
widen each other (products from any of them). Empty with a source other than `all` renders nothing.

fields.name: filterNew
fields.description:
`products` only. `yes` keeps only new products, `no` leaves them out, `both` (and null) does not
filter. Ignored by `productSource: product`.

fields.name: filterSale
fields.description: `products` only. The same three values as `filterNew`, for products on sale.

fields.name: filterFeatured
fields.description: `products` only. The same three values as `filterNew`, for the products the merchant marked featured.

fields.name: productSort
fields.description:
`products` only. The order: `bestSelling`, `newest`, `oldest`, `nameAsc`, `nameDesc`,
`priceAsc` or `priceDesc`. `default` (and null, and unknown values) means best selling for
`all`, and the store's own order for any other source. Ignored by `productSource: product`,
which keeps the merchant's picked order.

fields.name: items
fields.description:
`banner` and `bannerList` (and `banners` for a schema-1 client). The banners, in order. An empty list is legal — a campaign the
merchant is still assembling — and should render nothing rather than an empty strip.

The two types hold the same items and differ only in how they are laid out: `banners` shows one
at a time behind a swipe, `bannerList` shows all of them at once, `columns` per row, with each
item's `caption` under it.

fields.name: autoplay
fields.description: `banner` (with more than one item), `banners` and `video`. Whether it advances or plays on its own.

fields.name: interval
fields.description: `banner` and `banners`. Seconds per slide, 3-30. Ignored when `autoplay` is false.

fields.name: endsAt
fields.description:
`countdown` only. When it ends, UTC ISO-8601. Hide the whole section once it has passed —
a row of zeroes reads as a broken app, not as a finished promotion.

fields.name: content
fields.description:
`html` only. Already sanitised server-side against a narrow allowlist; render it as rich text,
never in a WebView.

fields.name: maxHeight
fields.description: `html` only. Maximum height in pixels. Null means as tall as the content.

fields.name: url
fields.description: `video` only. A hosted MP4 or HLS stream for the platform's own player. Never an embed page.

fields.name: poster

types.name: CartAttributionInput
types.description:
Where the buyer came from.

Two ways to say it, and most clients have at least one.

Give `landingUrl` and `referrer` whenever the entry point is a URL — a web
page, a deep link into an app, an install referrer. The platform then derives
everything else with the same classifier the merchant's own storefront uses:
UTM parameters, Google Ads and Meta click ids, and the traffic grouping the
merchant's reporting is built on. That is the better path: one URL yields more
than the three fields below ever could.

Where there is genuinely no such URL, name the campaign directly with the
`utm*` fields.

Both may be given. Explicit fields win over anything read from the URL, so use
them to correct rather than to repeat.

Attach this as soon as the cart exists, not at checkout. The buyer's origin
belongs to the visit that started the journey, and by the payment step it is
long gone.

inputFields.name: landingUrl
inputFields.description:
The full URL the buyer entered through, query string included. UTM
parameters, `gclid`, `fbclid` and the rest are read from it. A deep link or
an install referrer counts — anything that carries the campaign in a URL.

inputFields.name: referrer
inputFields.description: Where the buyer came from, when the client knows it — a browser's `document.referrer`, or the equivalent.

inputFields.name: utmSource
inputFields.description: The campaign source, when the client holds it as a value rather than inside a URL.

inputFields.name: utmMedium
inputFields.description: The campaign medium.

inputFields.name: utmCampaign
inputFields.description: The campaign name.

inputFields.name: visitorId
inputFields.description:
The visitor identifier issued by `visitorSessionCreate`. Any client can
hold one — it is not a cookie, and a mobile app should persist it exactly
as a browser would.

inputFields.name: searchTerm
inputFields.description:
The last phrase the buyer searched for with Aura Search (the phrase `predictiveSearch` answered with
`engine: aura`), so the order counts as coming from search in the merchant's Aura reports — what the
web storefront records in its session on every search-as-you-type.

inputFields.name: searchedAt
inputFields.description:
When that search happened. Defaults to now. Kept only with `searchTerm`;
without one it is ignored, with a warning.

Collect from a courier office or parcel locker instead of delivering to the

The name, phone and any company details are still collected — only the

The saved address supplies the destination; any other field sent alongside

different phone number without editing the address itself.

out between choosing and submitting.

types.description: Input for adding a line item to a cart.

inputFields.name: merchandiseId
inputFields.description: The ID of the merchandise (variant).

inputFields.name: quantity
inputFields.description: The quantity, at least 1.

inputFields.name: customizations
inputFields.description:
The buyer's answers to the product's customizations, listed by
`product.customizations`.

These are part of what identifies the line. The same variant added twice
with different answers becomes two lines; added twice with the same answers
it becomes one line of quantity two. They also change what the line costs,
so the price comes back in the response rather than being calculable here.
An answer that cannot be applied is dropped, with a warning: a
`customizationId` that is not an id or that the store has no customization
for, a `value` sent beside `values`, or a customization answered twice (the
later answer is kept). At most 100.

inputFields.name: sellingPlanId
inputFields.description:
Buy this line on a subscription, by the id of one of the product's
`sellingPlanGroups[].plans[]`.

Part of the line's identity: the same variant bought once and subscribed to
is two lines, at two prices, and they never merge. The plan is re-checked
against the variant on the server — a plan configured for another product is
refused, not silently dropped — and it changes what the line costs, so read
the price back from the response.

A cart that carries one may only be paid by a provider that can charge the
saved card again, and only by a registered customer; see
`cartCheckoutReadiness`.

inputFields.name: upSellTriggerVariantId
inputFields.description:
The trigger variant of the up-sell (`upSellOffer`) the buyer took: the
line is the offer variant, at the offer's price, and the merchant's up-sell
statistics count it. Applied only when that trigger has one active up-sell
and this line's variant is its offer variant; otherwise the line is added at
its own price, with a warning.

inputFields.name: crossSellId
inputFields.description:
The cross-sell offer (`CrossSellOffer.id`) this line came from: the line gets
the offer's price when the cart holds the offer's trigger products, and the
merchant's statistics count it. Only a `POPUP` offer is taken this way. When
the offer is not active, is not one the API shows, does not apply to the
line, or the cart already holds this variant without it, the line is added at
its own price, with a warning.

types.description: One answer to a product customization.

inputFields.name: customizationId
inputFields.description: The customization, from `product.customizations`.

inputFields.name: value
inputFields.description:
The answer, for the types that take a single one: the chosen value's id for
`select`, `radio` and `checkbox`; the text for `text` and `textarea`; the
number above zero for `weight` and `length` (anything else refuses the line
with `INVALID`); for `file`, the `handle` that
`cartCustomizationFileUpload` returned. A handle is used once: adding the
line moves the file into the cart. A handle that cannot be used (expired,
used, or not this customization's) refuses the line with `INVALID`, and the
file must be uploaded again.

inputFields.name: values
inputFields.description:
The answers, for a customization that takes several: the chosen value ids
when `multiple` is set, or length and width in that order for `square` —
two numbers above zero, or both left blank for no answer; anything else
refuses the line with `INVALID`.

types.name: CartLineUpdateInput
types.description:
Input for updating a cart line.

There is no free-form data on a line. Anything attached to a line has to reach
the order, be priced, and appear on the picking list, and the platform's way of
doing that is a product customization the merchant configured — see
`product.customizations`. Arbitrary line properties would have nowhere to go.

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description: The ID of the cart line to update.

inputFields.name: quantity
inputFields.description: The new quantity.

inputFields.name: merchandiseId
inputFields.description:
The new merchandise ID. The line keeps its customizations, as this input takes none: onto another
product, the swap is refused with `MISSING_CUSTOMIZATION` when that product's required customizations
are not among them, and with `INVALID` when the line answers a customization that product does not
ask. Remove the line and add the new one instead.

inputFields.name: sellingPlanId
inputFields.description:
Change the subscription plan, or send `null` to turn the line back into a
one-time purchase.

Omitting the field leaves the line's plan alone — but changing
`merchandiseId` re-checks it, and a plan that does not apply to the new
variant is dropped rather than carried across to a variant it was never
approved for.

types.name: CartBuyerIdentityInput
types.description:
Who is buying.

A cart starts with nobody attached and may stay that way. Identity can arrive
at any moment and in any order — sign in first, type an email halfway through,
or stay anonymous until the last step. Every field is optional and each may be
sent on its own.

A customer record is only created once there is an email to create it from.
Anything sent before that — a phone, a name — is held against the cart and
folded in when an email or a sign-in gives it an owner, so nothing is lost by
sending it early.

inputFields.name: email
inputFields.description:
The buyer's email. This is what identifies a guest: sending it attaches a
guest customer to the cart, reusing an existing one for the same address
rather than creating a second. On a cart signed in as a customer it is
ignored, with a warning: the customer keeps the email they signed in with.

inputFields.name: phone
inputFields.description:
The buyer's phone number. Held against the cart until there is a customer to
put it on. On a cart signed in as a customer it is saved only when the
customer has no phone; otherwise it is ignored, with a warning.

inputFields.name: firstName
inputFields.description:
The buyer's first name. On a cart signed in as a customer it is ignored,
with a warning: the name in the account is kept.

inputFields.name: lastName
inputFields.description:
The buyer's last name. On a cart signed in as a customer it is ignored, with
a warning: the name in the account is kept.

inputFields.name: countryCode
inputFields.description:
Ignored, with a warning: a CloudCart cart keeps no buyer country, because a
store serves one country.

inputFields.name: customerAccessToken

identified earlier on the same cart — a guest created from a typed email is
a placeholder for exactly this. An invalid or expired token is refused
rather than ignored.

Answers to the merchant's own questions about the buyer, listed by
`checkoutSettings.customFields`.

This replaces every answer the buyer has given, so send the complete set
each time — omitting a field clears it rather than leaving it alone.

Sent before there is a customer to hold them, the answers wait on the cart
and are recorded once an email or a sign-in identifies the buyer.

inputFields.name: acceptsMarketing
inputFields.description: Whether the customer accepts marketing.

types.name: MailingAddressInput
types.description:
A customer's delivery or billing address.

The store decides which fields are asked for and which are required: read
`checkoutSettings.fields` and build the form from it. The address is checked
against those settings and refused with one `CustomerUserError` per field,
`field` being `["address", "<input field>"]`.

On an update, only the fields sent change; a field sent empty is cleared. The
rules apply to the address as it will be saved.

inputFields.name: address1
inputFields.description: The street. Send the house number in `streetNumber` when the store asks for it separately.

inputFields.name: streetNumber
inputFields.description: The house or building number.

inputFields.name: address2
inputFields.description: Additional address detail: apartment, floor, entrance.

inputFields.name: city
inputFields.description: The city.

inputFields.name: countryCode
inputFields.description:
The two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). It must be one of
`localization.availableCountries`. Takes precedence over `country`.

inputFields.name: country
inputFields.description: The country's name, or its two-letter code. Prefer `countryCode`.

inputFields.name: firstName
inputFields.description: The first name.

inputFields.name: lastName
inputFields.description: The last name.

inputFields.name: phone
inputFields.description: The phone number, checked against the address's country and stored in international (E.164) form, as the platform stores every address's phone.

inputFields.name: province
inputFields.description: The province, region or state. Sending it or `provinceCode` replaces both.

inputFields.name: provinceCode
inputFields.description: The province, region or state code. Sending it or `province` replaces both.

inputFields.name: zip
inputFields.description: The postal or ZIP code.

inputFields.name: company
inputFields.description: The company name. Asked for on billing addresses.

inputFields.name: companyVat
inputFields.description:
The company VAT number. Asked for on billing addresses. Within the EU it is
confirmed with VIES when the store has `checkoutSettings.fields.validateCompanyVat`
on, and refused when VIES does not confirm it.

inputFields.name: companyBulstat
inputFields.description: The company's registration number (Bulgarian EIK/BULSTAT). Billing addresses only; ignored on a delivery address.

inputFields.name: companyMol
inputFields.description: The company's responsible person (Bulgarian MOL). Billing addresses only; ignored on a delivery address.

types.name: ReturnLineItemInput
types.description: An item the customer wants to include in a return.

inputFields.name: lineItemId
inputFields.description:
The order line to return, as given by `OrderLineItem.id`. Lines are identified per-order, so the same
product bought twice with different options can be returned independently.

inputFields.name: quantity

types.name: ReturnRefundInput

inputFields.name: method

The payout method, chosen from `ReturnEligibility.refundMethods`. The store validates the choice
server-side and falls back to its default when the method is not offered.

inputFields.name: accountName

inputFields.name: iban
inputFields.description: The IBAN to refund to. Required when refunding to a bank account.

inputFields.name: bic

types.name: AnalyticsEventInput
types.description: What happened, and everything known about who it happened to.

inputFields.name: cartId
inputFields.description: The cart the event concerns.

inputFields.name: orderId
inputFields.description:
The order the event concerns, for a purchase. Read only when the operation
runs for the order's own customer (`@inContext(buyer)`): its lines, total
and e-mail then go to the ad platforms. Anyone else's order, a guest's
included, is ignored, and the event is sent without order data.

inputFields.name: visitorId
inputFields.description:
The visitor identifier from `visitorSessionCreate`. Meta refuses an event
it cannot tie to anyone, and CloudCart Analytics records visits by it, so
without this nothing is sent server-side.

inputFields.name: consentedGroups
inputFields.description:
The consent groups the buyer has accepted. The platform's consent rules
then decide what each vendor may receive; a group not listed counts as its
default (`analyticsSettings.consentGroups[].acceptedByDefault`).

inputFields.name: refusedGroups
inputFields.description:
The consent groups the buyer has refused. Each counts as refused whatever
its default, as on the merchant's own storefront, and a refusal wins over
the same group in `consentedGroups`. A group in neither list counts as its
default.

inputFields.name: url
inputFields.description: The page the event happened on.

inputFields.name: userAgent
inputFields.description: The buyer's browser user agent, where the client knows it.

inputFields.name: fbp
inputFields.description: Meta's browser cookie, where the client has it.

inputFields.name: fbc
inputFields.description: Meta's click identifier, where the client has it.

inputFields.name: ttclid
inputFields.description: TikTok's click identifier, where the client has it.

inputFields.name: ttp
inputFields.description: TikTok's browser cookie, where the client has it.

inputFields.name: pageType
inputFields.description: The kind of page, for `PAGE_VIEW`.

inputFields.name: resourceId
inputFields.description:
What the event is about: the viewed product (`VIEW_CONTENT`, wishlist
events), or the category, collection, tag, vendor or page (`PAGE_VIEW`).

inputFields.name: merchandiseId
inputFields.description: The product variant added to or removed from the cart.

inputFields.name: quantity
inputFields.description:
How many were added (`ADD_TO_CART`) or removed (`REMOVE_FROM_CART`). The
line's whole quantity when not given.

inputFields.name: searchTerm
inputFields.description: The search terms, for `SEARCH`.

inputFields.name: referrer
inputFields.description:
The page the visitor came from: on the first page of a visit the browser's
`document.referrer`, after that the storefront page before this one — what
`document.referrer` would be had each page been loaded in full. It decides
the traffic source in the merchant's reports.

inputFields.name: pageTitle
inputFields.description: The page's title.

inputFields.name: eventId
inputFields.description:
The identifier the browser's pixels reported this event under: 32
hexadecimal characters, as the merchant's own storefront makes them. Meta
and TikTok count an event once when the browser and the server share it.
Any other value is ignored, and the API makes one and returns it. A
checkout with `cartId` and a purchase with `orderId` take the identifier
derived from the cart or the order instead (`AnalyticsEventPayload.eventId`).

inputFields.name: reportedInBrowser
inputFields.description:
The vendors the browser already sent this event to. A vendor that cannot
tell the two apart (Google Analytics: the Measurement Protocol adds to what
the browser sends) is then not sent it from the server; Meta and TikTok
still are, and count it once by `eventId`.

inputFields.name: customerEmailHash
inputFields.description:
The signed-in customer's e-mail, trimmed, lower-cased and SHA-256 hashed
(64 hexadecimal characters), for Meta to match the event to them. Never the
e-mail itself. An order's own e-mail (`orderId`) takes precedence.

The objects with these global IDs, in the order asked, each as its type's
