merchant's hand-picked products, in one call instead of one per ID. Null in
the place of an ID of another kind, a plain ID without its type, or an
object the storefront does not show. At most 100 IDs; IDs of one type load
together, whatever their number.

fields.name: recentlyViewedProducts
fields.description:
The products a visitor viewed, most recent first — for a "recently viewed"
block. The storefront keeps the list itself, in the visitor's browser; this
turns it into products, keeping its order and leaving out any no longer on
the storefront.

args.name: productIds
args.description: The viewed products' ids, most recent first.

args.name: first
args.description: How many to return: 8 unless given, at most 30.

fields.name: productComparison
fields.description:
Compares products, as the platform's compare page does. The storefront keeps
the visitor's choice itself; only the first three ids are compared, the
platform's limit.

args.name: productIds
args.description: The products' ids, in the order to show them.

fields.name: productTag
fields.description:
Find a product tag by ID or handle — the tag page, `/tags/{handle}`. A
handle the tag had before it was renamed still finds it; compare the
returned `handle` and redirect when it differs.

fields.name: product
fields.description: Find a product by ID or handle.

fields.name: products
fields.description:
Get a paginated list of products. Order by default: `ID`, oldest product
first, also with `query` (pass `sortKey: RELEVANCE` to rank by the search).
When the merchant lists products that cannot be bought last, they come after
the others in every order.

args.name: sortKey
args.description: What to order by. Omitted: with a `query` by relevance, without one in the store's own listing order — its listing setting, or best sellers first when it set none.

args.name: reverse
args.description: Turns the key's order around: newest, Z to A, dearest or least sold first. No effect without a key, or with `RELEVANCE`, `PRODUCT_TYPE` or `VENDOR`.

args.name: filters
args.description: Filter products by availability, price, vendor, tag, or variant option.

args.name: smartFacetCounts
args.description: Whether to compute smart facet counts via cross-filter aggregations. Disable for faster responses when exact counts are not needed.

fields.name: productRecommendations
fields.description: Get product recommendations for a given product.

fields.name: productReviewSettings
fields.description:
The merchant's settings for product reviews, or null when the store does not run the
Product Reviews app — then products have no reviews to show.

fields.name: vendor
fields.description: Find a vendor by ID or handle.

fields.name: vendors
fields.description:
Vendors by ID, in the order asked — for a client handed vendor IDs by the
merchant, such as the mobile app's brands section. Global IDs and the plain
numeric IDs the merchant's settings hold are both read. An ID with no vendor
is skipped rather than returned as null; at most 100 IDs are read.

Kept as a plain list for the clients built against it; `vendorsConnection`
pages through the same vendors, or through every vendor with products.

fields.name: vendorsConnection
fields.description:
The vendors that have at least one active, published product — what a
storefront's brands page lists. Vendors without a name are left out. With
`ids`, those vendors instead (see `vendors`). Order: by name, A to Z; with
`ids`, the order they were asked in.

args.name: ids
args.description: Only these vendors, in this order. Global IDs or the plain numeric IDs the merchant's settings hold.

fields.name: collection
fields.description: Find a collection by ID or handle.

args.name: kind
args.description:
Only a collection of this kind is returned; null when the id or handle
belongs to the other kind. Omitted, a handle finds a category first and
then a smart collection, so a smart collection whose handle a category
also uses is reached only with `SMART_COLLECTION`.

fields.name: collections
fields.description:
Get a paginated list of the store's categories, or with `kind: SMART_COLLECTION`
its smart collections; for both, ask twice under two aliases. Order by default:
newest first (`ID`). Every key but `MANUAL` lists in descending order — Z to A for `TITLE`,
latest update first for `UPDATED_AT` — and `reverse: true` lists in ascending
order; `MANUAL` lists in the merchant's order and `reverse` the other way.

The store's own categories page lists `topLevel: true, withProducts: true,
sortKey: MANUAL`.

args.name: sortKey
args.description: What to order by. Defaults to `ID`.

args.name: reverse
args.description: Ascending order instead: oldest, A to Z, or least recently updated first.

args.name: topLevel
args.description: Only the categories without a parent. A smart collection has none, so all of them.

args.name: withProducts
args.description:
Only the collections with products, as the store's listing engine counts
them: a category's in it or in a category under it, a smart collection's own.

args.name: kind
args.description: Which collections to list: omitted or `CATEGORY` the categories, `SMART_COLLECTION` the smart collections.

fields.name: cartCheckoutReadiness
fields.description:
Whether the cart can be submitted, and what is missing when it cannot.

Read this before showing the buyer a submit button. Every requirement is
something the server will refuse without, named so the checkout can point
at the field that needs attention rather than reporting a bare failure.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

fields.name: cartPickupPoints
fields.description:
Courier offices or parcel lockers the buyer can collect from.

Every courier searches its own network, so this is a live lookup across all
couriers in the chosen group. Pass a `query` — a bare city name can match
hundreds of points — and pass `carrierHandle` once the buyer has settled on
a courier.

Points that cannot take the cart's weight are left out: the checkout
applies the same rule, so offering one would only fail later.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart. Its weight and geo zone narrow the search.

args.name: type
args.description: Whether to search courier offices or parcel lockers.

args.name: query
args.description: Free text matched against the point's name, city and address.

args.name: carrierHandle
args.description: Restrict the search to one courier.

args.name: first
args.description: How many points to return. Defaults to 25, maximum 100.

fields.name: cartDeliverySlots
fields.description:
The delivery time slots a courier offers.

Empty for most couriers. When a courier does return slots, choosing one is
mandatory — submitting the order without it is refused — so ask for these
after the buyer picks the courier and pass the chosen key to
`cartSelectedDeliveryOptionUpdate`.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

args.name: carrierHandle
args.description: The courier to ask, from cart.delivery.carriers.

fields.name: upSellOffer
fields.description:
The up-sell the store proposes when this variant is added, or null when there
is none or the Up/Cross-sell app is not active. Read it before adding the
variant: if there is one, the buyer chooses between the two. An up-sell whose
offer variant the cart already holds is not proposed, and neither is any when
the merchant has more than one active up-sell for the variant, since the store
could price the line by either.

args.name: variantId
args.description: The variant about to be added.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The buyer's cart, when there is one.

fields.name: cartCreditPlans
fields.description:
The instalment plans a credit provider offers for this cart.

Only for methods whose `group` is CREDIT, and only for methods the cart may
actually use. Anything else returns an empty list.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

args.name: downPayment
args.description: A down payment the buyer wants to make, in major units. Changes every plan.

fields.name: cart
fields.description: Retrieve a cart by its ID.

fields.name: customer
fields.description: Retrieve the authenticated customer.

fields.name: order
fields.description: Retrieve a single order by ID for the authenticated customer.

fields.name: page
fields.description: Find a page by ID or handle. Null for an inactive page, as the store's own page answers 404 for it, and for a page-builder page, which this API does not serve (see `Page`).

fields.name: pages
fields.description:
Get a paginated list of the store's active pages. Page-builder pages are not
included (see `Page`). Order by default: newest first (`ID`). Every key
lists in descending order — Z to A for `TITLE`, latest update first for
`UPDATED_AT` — and `reverse: true` lists in ascending order.

args.name: sortKey
args.description: What to order by. Defaults to `ID`.

args.name: reverse
args.description: Ascending order instead: oldest, A to Z, or least recently updated first.

fields.name: blog
fields.description: Find a blog by ID or handle.

fields.name: blogs
fields.description:
Get a paginated list of blogs. Order by default: newest first (`ID`). Every
key lists in descending order — Z to A for `TITLE` — and `reverse: true`
lists in ascending order.

args.name: sortKey
args.description: What to order by. Defaults to `ID`.

args.name: reverse
args.description: Ascending order instead: oldest, or A to Z, first.

fields.name: article
fields.description:
Find an article by ID or handle, in whichever blog it is filed. The
platform's article address, `/article/{handle}`, carries no blog, so this is
how a storefront opens it. Null for an article that is hidden or not yet
published.

fields.name: articles
fields.description:
The published articles of every blog — what the platform shows at `/blog`.
Order by default: newest first (`ID`). Every key lists in descending order —
Z to A for `TITLE`, latest first for `PUBLISHED_AT` — and `reverse: true`
lists in ascending order.

args.name: sortKey
args.description: What to order by. Defaults to `ID`.

args.name: reverse
args.description: Ascending order instead: oldest, A to Z, or earliest published first.

args.name: query
args.description:
Filters, in Shopify's search syntax: `tag:` (an article tag's text),
`tag_not:` and `blog_title:`, e.g. `tag:summer` or
`blog_title:"Style tips" tag_not:archive`. Quote a value that has
spaces. Several filters, separated by spaces or `AND`, must all match;
a filter of any other kind matches no article.

fields.name: articleTag
fields.description:
Find an article tag by ID or handle — the tag page, `/blog/tag/{handle}`,
with the articles that carry the tag.

fields.name: menu
fields.description: Find a menu by handle.

fields.name: policies
fields.description:
The store's policies, required ones first. Without the GDPR app, the store's
checkout terms pages (the terms page and the other checkout pages the merchant
chose), each required on `SUBMIT_PAYMENT`; nothing on the other forms.

args.name: form
args.description: Only the policies asked on this form.

fields.name: urlRedirects
fields.description:
The store's URL redirects. Order: oldest first; `reverse: true` lists the
newest first.

To find where a visitor who opened an address should be sent — what a
storefront does before answering "not found" — pass `query:
"path:/old-address"`, without a trailing slash. The result then holds the
one redirect the platform storefront follows for that address — one entered
as the address itself, as the address with a trailing slash, or as a `*`
pattern that covers it — or nothing.

args.name: first
args.description: Returns up to the first n redirects.

args.name: after
args.description: Returns the redirects after this cursor.

args.name: last
args.description: Returns up to the last n redirects.

args.name: before
args.description: Returns the redirects before this cursor.

args.name: query
args.description:
A filter. `path:` is the only one supported, e.g. `path:/old-address` or
`path:"/old address"`; anything else matches no redirect.

args.name: reverse
args.description: Newest first instead of oldest first.

fields.name: analyticsSettings
fields.description:
Which marketing pixels this store runs and what consent they need.

Read it once when your storefront boots. Note that suppressing tracking
for staff is your own concern: this API has no admin session and cannot
tell whose browser is asking.

fields.name: checkoutSettings
fields.description:
The checkout configuration of this store — which fields are collected, who
may check out, what consents are required and which custom fields to ask
for. Read it once when the checkout mounts; it changes only when the
merchant changes their settings.

fields.name: cookieConsent
fields.description:
The cookie consent banner, as the merchant set it up in the GDPR app: a bar
or a wall, its texts, and the consent groups with the cookies each covers.
A change in the admin shows here at once.

`active` is false when the GDPR app is not active: then the store asks for
no consent, and shows no banner.

fields.name: fastOrderSettings
fields.description:
The merchant's Fast Order settings, or null when Fast Order must not be
offered: the app is off or not configured, the store's plan has no
checkout, or cash on delivery is unavailable.

Show the product-page button only when this is not null. The consents to
ask for and the order value limits are in `checkoutSettings`.

fields.name: mobileAppConfig
fields.description:
The merchant's design for this store's native mobile app.

Public branding, at the same trust level as `shop` — read-only, and unauthenticated
beyond the storefront token. Read it once at boot, cache it, and re-render when
`version` changes.

Always answers. An unconfigured store returns nulls throughout rather than an error,
which is what lets a client fall back to its own compiled defaults field by field.

args.name: schema
args.description:
The shape of the config this client reads. Omit it and you get schema 1, the shape apps were
built against before the argument existed: `hero` and `banners` sections instead of `banner`,
and one `showSku` for the SKU, the barcode and the weight. Pass 2 for the current shape.

fields.name: mobileAppPage
fields.description:
One of the app's landing pages (`mobileAppConfig.pages`), with its sections. Null for a page that
does not exist (deleted since the link was made): show an empty state.

args.name: id
args.description: The page's id, as `MobileAppPageRef.id` and a tab's or a link's `value` give it.

fields.name: shop
fields.description: The shop associated with the storefront access token.

fields.name: localization
fields.description: Localization information for the current context.

fields.name: storeLocation
fields.description: Fetch a single physical store / pickup location by ID or URL handle.

args.name: id
args.description: The store's global ID (or raw numeric ID).

fields.name: storeLocations
fields.description: List the merchant's physical store / pickup locations.

fields.name: subscribeForms
fields.description:
The store's pop-up subscribe forms — up to five active ones, as the platform's
storefront loads them. Each says when and where it opens (`display`), whether
it waits for marketing consent, and whether it is for this visitor at all
(`showToSubscribers`, `visitorIsSubscribed`).

args.name: visitorId
args.description:
The visitor, as `visitorSessionCreate` issued it, so a visitor the store
already has as a subscriber is recognised. Not needed for a signed-in
customer.

fields.name: subscribeForm
fields.description: A subscribe form by id, embedded or pop-up — for placing an embedded form in a page. Null when it is not active.

fields.name: translations
fields.description: The label bundle the native storefront app renders its UI from, in the store's language.

fields.name: search
fields.description:
Search the store for products, pages and articles; pagination runs across
all three. Order: products first, as the search engine ranks them (the
merchant's search pins on top) or by `sortKey`; then pages, oldest first;
then articles, newest first.

args.name: sortKey
args.description: What to order the products by. Defaults to `RELEVANCE`, the search engine's rank; `PRODUCT_TYPE` and `VENDOR` keep it too.

args.name: reverse
args.description: Turns the products' order around for `TITLE`, `PRICE`, `BEST_SELLING`, `CREATED_AT`, `UPDATED_AT` or `ID`: newest, Z to A, dearest or least sold first. Pages and articles keep their order.

args.name: unavailableProducts
args.description:
How products that cannot be bought are treated. Left out, the store's own
settings decide, as they do on its web storefront. A store that hides such
products keeps them hidden whatever is asked.

args.name: smartFacetCounts
args.description: Whether to compute smart facet counts via cross-filter aggregations.

fields.name: predictiveSearch
fields.description: Suggested results as the customer types: products, collections, pages and articles.

args.name: limit
args.description: The most results to return, per type or in all depending on `limitScope`. Defaults to 10, at most 25.

args.name: limitScope
args.description: Whether `limit` applies to each type or to all of them together. Defaults to EACH.

args.name: types
args.description: Limit the search to these types. Defaults to all of them.

args.name: unavailableProducts
args.description:
How products that cannot be bought are treated. Left out, the store's own
settings decide. A store that hides such products keeps them hidden.

fields.name: draftOrder
fields.description:
Opens an order the merchant prepared for the buyer to pay.

A merchant can build an order in the admin — a quote, a phone order, an
invoice — and send the customer a link. On the merchant's own storefront
that link opens a platform page; a headless storefront reads it here and
renders it itself.

The `hash` is the one carried in the link. It is the only thing protecting
someone else's order, so anything that does not match returns null rather
than explaining why.

Returns null once the order is paid, cancelled or already shipped.

args.name: id
args.description: The order's identifier, as it appears in the link.

fields.name: orderStatus
fields.description:
Where one order stands, readable WITHOUT a customer account.

`order(customerAccessToken:)` covers a shopper who signed in, and most CloudCart storefront
orders are placed by a guest — so a headless client had no way at all to re-read the order it had
just created. Two things needed exactly that: a client returning from a payment provider, which
has to ask the store what the payment actually did rather than trust the URL the browser landed
on, and an app confirming that the order it bound to a push device is real.

Ownership is proved by the email the order was placed with, which is the same proof the
merchant's own order-status page asks a guest for. It is not a session: this returns the STATUS of
an order and nothing that identifies the buyer — no address, no line items, no contact details —
so a wrong guess reveals nothing beyond whether that pair exists.

Returns null for an unknown id, a mismatched email and an order belonging to a signed-in-only
flow alike: a client cannot tell which, and that is deliberate.

args.name: id
args.description: The order id, as returned by `cartSubmitForCompletion`.

args.name: email
args.description: The email address the order was placed with.

fields.name: returnByReference
fields.description:
Look up a return by its public reference — the value carried by the tracking link in the notification
emails. Requires no sign-in, so it exposes only what the customer already received by email.

fields.name: returnRequestFlow
fields.description:
The return flow a token carries, as its last mutation left it: `AWAITING_CODE` until the code is
verified, then `VERIFIED` with the order and what may go back. Null for an unknown or expired token.
Keep only the token between requests and read the flow here, rather than holding a copy of it: a copy
sent back by the browser can be changed. Reading counts no attempt and sends no code.

fields.name: metaobject
fields.description: A metaobject by its id, or by its type and handle; null when the storefront does not show it.

fields.name: metaobjects
fields.description:
The metaobjects of a type the storefront shows: of a definition whose storefront access is `PUBLIC_READ`, and
of one with the active-draft status only the active entries. Empty for any other type. Order by default: by
id, the oldest first; with `sortKey: "updated_at"`, by the last update, then by id. With `query`, only the
entries whose fields match it, in the same order.

args.name: first
args.description: Returns up to the first n elements from the list.

args.name: after
args.description: Returns the elements that come after the specified cursor.

args.name: last
args.description: Returns up to the last n elements from the list.

args.name: before
args.description: Returns the elements that come before the specified cursor.

args.name: reverse
args.description: Turns the order around: the newest first, or the latest update first.

args.name: sortKey
args.description: The key to sort by: `id` (the default) or `updated_at`.

args.name: query
args.description:
Filters by the type's fields that have the admin filter on, in Shopify's search syntax: `fields.{key}:{value}`,
e.g. `fields.color:blue`, `fields.on_sale:true`, `fields.year:>=2020 -fields.tags:"sale"`. A text matches
exactly and case-sensitively, or by a prefix with `*`; numbers, measurements and dates take `>`, `>=`, `<`,
`<=`; a reference matches by its global id; a list matches when any of its items does; `fields.{key}:*` means
has a value, and `-` or `NOT` negates. A term this list cannot filter by — another field, a field without the
admin filter, a value its type cannot hold, free text — is ignored, as Shopify ignores an invalid search field.
A query longer, or with more terms or nested groups, than the search syntax allows is refused with an error.
A CloudCart addition: Shopify's Storefront API has no filter on this list.

types.name: Mutation
types.description: The schema's entry point for mutations: everything a storefront changes.

fields.name: cartAttributionUpdate
fields.description:
Records where the buyer came from, so the order carries the same
attribution a browser checkout would.

A GraphQL request has no session and no landing page of its own, so
nothing can be inferred — without this call the order is recorded with no
source at all, and the merchant's reporting shows it as direct traffic.

Call it once, as early as the cart exists. Calling it again replaces what
was stored.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

fields.name: cartSubmitForCompletion
fields.description:
Turns the cart into an order.

Check `cartCheckoutReadiness` first — this refuses anything it reports as
missing, and says which. Pass the ids of every consent the buyer accepted;
a headless storefront must send them explicitly, because nothing else
records that the buyer agreed.

`attemptToken` makes the call safe to retry: the same token always returns
the same order rather than creating a second one. Generate one per
checkout attempt and reuse it if the call fails or times out.

Cards finish at the provider. Those return REQUIRES_REDIRECT with the URL
to send the buyer to — the order already exists and is awaiting payment.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

args.name: attemptToken
args.description: A token identifying this attempt. Reuse it when retrying.

args.name: input
args.description: What the buyer supplied at the final step.

fields.name: cartDeliveryAddressUpdate
fields.description:
Sets where the order is going.

CloudCart keeps one delivery address per cart, so this replaces whatever
was there. Which fields are required depends on the store — read
`checkoutSettings.fields` rather than assuming.

Changing the destination invalidates every price already quoted for it.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

fields.name: cartDeliveryAddressRemove
fields.description: Clears the cart's delivery address, along with any prices quoted for it.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

fields.name: cartDeliveryQuote
fields.description:
Asks one courier for its prices and stores them on the cart.

Call this once per courier from `cart.delivery.carriers`, issuing the calls
in parallel. Quoting is a live request to the courier: most answer in
milliseconds, but a single slow courier can take seconds, and asking them
one after another would make the buyer wait for the sum rather than for the
slowest.

A courier that fails or has no service to the destination returns no
options and no error — it simply has nothing to offer.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

args.name: carrierHandle
args.description: The courier to ask, from cart.delivery.carriers.

fields.name: cartSelectedDeliveryOptionUpdate
fields.description:
Chooses the delivery service for the cart.

The option must already be quoted — completing the order resolves the
choice against the stored prices, so an unquoted handle is refused.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

args.name: optionHandle
args.description: The option handle, from a carrier's options.

args.name: deliverySlotKey
args.description:
The chosen time slot, for couriers that require one. See
cartDeliverySlots. A key that is not one of the service's slots is
stored but not used by the order, with a warning.

fields.name: cartOfferViewed
fields.description:
Counts that an offer was shown to the buyer, in the merchant's statistics.
The storefront also adds the view to the buyer's `OfferHistoryInput`. A visitor
may count 30 views a minute; past that the answer is `THROTTLED`.

args.name: offerId
args.description: The offer's `id`: one the API shows (`crossSellOffer`, `upSellOffer` or one they lead to); any other is refused.

fields.name: cartOfferDismissed
fields.description:
Counts that the buyer dismissed an offer, in the merchant's statistics. The
storefront also adds it to the buyer's `OfferHistoryInput`, so it is not shown again.
A visitor may count 30 dismissals a minute; past that the answer is `THROTTLED`.

args.name: offerId
args.description: The offer's `id`: one the API shows, as for `cartOfferViewed`.

fields.name: cartCrossSellApply
fields.description:
Adds the products of the cart page's `ADD_TO_CART` cross-sell (`cart.crossSellOffer`)
to the cart, at the offer's price, as the store's own cart page does. An offer
the cart no longer meets, or whose products are all in the cart already, adds
nothing, with a warning.

fields.name: cartPaymentMethodUpdate
fields.description:
Chooses how the order will be paid.

Only a method listed in `cart.paymentMethods` is accepted — that list is
already filtered by everything the server checks, so anything outside it
would be refused at submission anyway.

When the chosen method has `recalculatesShipping`, re-read the cart
afterwards: the courier may reprice the delivery.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

args.name: creditPlanId
args.description:
The instalment plan, for a CREDIT method. Required for those — see
cartCreditPlans. With another method it is ignored, with a warning.

args.name: downPayment
args.description:
The down payment agreed with the plan, in major units. With a method
that is not CREDIT it is ignored, with a warning.

fields.name: cartPaymentSessionCreate
fields.description:
Opens a session for collecting card details inside your own checkout.

Available only for a cart whose chosen method supports it — today that is
CloudCart Pay, configured for inline display. Everything else answers with
an error, and those methods are completed by redirect instead.

Open the session after the payment method is chosen and shortly before the
buyer types their card: sessions are short-lived and are priced for the
cart as it stands.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

fields.name: cartCreate
fields.description:
Create a new cart. Its input is applied in order — lines, buyer identity,
discount codes, attributes — and stops at the first part that fails; the
parts sent after it are named in `warnings` as not applied.

args.name: offerHistory
args.description: The buyer's offer history, for the cross-sell picked after its lines are added (see `cartLinesAdd`).

fields.name: cartLinesAdd
fields.description:
Add lines to an existing cart.

After the add, the store's Up/Cross-sell app may pick a cross-sell for the lines
just added; it comes back as the payload's `crossSellOffer`.

A bundle's own variant is refused: a bundle is added whole, with a variant chosen for each of
its products, through `cartBundleAdd`. The same applies to `cartCreate`, and to the `line` of
`fastOrderSubmit`, which takes a bundle through its `bundle` input instead.

args.name: lines
args.description: The lines to add, at most 100.

args.name: offerHistory
args.description:
What the buyer has already seen and dismissed, for the cross-sell picked
after the add. Send it, even empty, when the storefront shows offers: only
then does the store pick one (`crossSellOffer`), and an `ADD_TO_CART` offer
add its products to the cart. Without it the add changes nothing else.

fields.name: cartLinesUpdate
fields.description: Update lines in a cart.

args.name: lines
args.description: The lines to update, at most 100.

args.name: offerHistory
args.description:
What the buyer has already seen and dismissed, for the cross-sell the store
picks after a quantity change, as after an add (`cartLinesAdd`).

fields.name: cartLinesRemove
fields.description: Remove lines from a cart.

args.name: lineIds
args.description: The IDs of the lines to remove, at most 100. An id that is not a line of this cart is skipped, with a warning.

fields.name: cartDiscountCodesUpdate
fields.description: Update discount codes on a cart.

fields.name: cartBuyerIdentityUpdate
fields.description: Update the buyer identity on a cart.

fields.name: cartCustomizationFileUpload
fields.description:
Upload a buyer's file for a `file` customization, before the line is added.
Send the request as `multipart/form-data` by the GraphQL multipart request
specification. The file is checked on its contents against the store's limits
(`ProductCustomization.fileUpload`). Send the returned `file.handle` as the
customization's value in `cartLinesAdd`, `cartCreate` or `cartBundleAdd`. One
visitor may upload 20 files a minute; past that the answer is `THROTTLED`.

args.name: customizationId
args.description: The `file` customization the file answers, from `product.customizations`.

fields.name: cartNoteUpdate
fields.description:
Kept for the clients built against it; changes nothing. A CloudCart cart has
no note — the buyer writes one for the merchant in the checkout, and it is
kept on the order. Returns the cart as it is, with a warning when a note is
sent.

fields.name: cartAttributesUpdate
fields.description: Update custom attributes on a cart.

fields.name: cartBundleAdd
fields.description:
Adds a bundle to the cart.

A bundle is a group, not a line: the cart ends up with one line per product
in it, all tied to the same group and priced together. Choose every product
in the bundle — a partial bundle is refused rather than part-filled — and
give each one's variant and any customizations, exactly as for a line.

Either the whole bundle is added or none of it is.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The global ID of the cart.

args.name: bundle
args.description: The bundle and the buyer's choices within it.

fields.name: customerCreate
fields.description:
Create a new customer account. A login code is automatically emailed to the address after creation.
A visitor may register 10 times a minute; past that the answer is `THROTTLED`.

fields.name: customerPolicyConsentAccept
fields.description:
Records that the signed-in customer accepted the store's policies, in answer to
`Customer.policyConsentRequest`. Every policy of the request that is required on
`POLICIES_POPUP` must be among `acceptedPolicyIds`; ids of other policies are refused.
Once a customer has accepted a policy, `policyConsentRequest` is null for them.

args.name: acceptedPolicyIds
args.description: The ids of the policies the customer accepted (`Policy.id` from `Customer.policyConsentRequest`), at most 100.

args.name: buyerUserAgent
args.description: The customer's browser user agent, for a storefront that calls the API from its own server.

fields.name: customerUpdate
fields.description: Update an existing customer.

fields.name: customerLoginCodeSend
fields.description:
Send a six-digit login code to the customer's email.

This is the only way to sign in through this API. There is deliberately no
password login and no password reset — the merchant's own storefront still
offers both, but a headless client would have to collect and forward a
password it has no business handling, and a one-time code is the stronger
check. A buyer who has a password signs in with a code instead; nothing
about their account changes.

Always succeeds, so the response cannot be used to discover which addresses
have accounts. A code is generated and sent only when the email matches an
active, non-guest customer. A pending code is mailed again, at most once a
minute per address. A visitor may ask 10 times a minute; past that the answer
is `THROTTLED`, for any address.

fields.name: customerLoginCodeVerify
fields.description:
Verify a login code and, on success, issue a customer access token. A code
takes 5 tries, right or wrong, and then stops working: ask for a new one with
`customerLoginCodeSend`. A wrong, used or expired code is `TOKEN_INVALID`; a
disabled account is `CUSTOMER_DISABLED`. A visitor may try 10 times a minute;
past that the answer is `THROTTLED`.

args.name: code
args.description: The six-digit code received by email.

fields.name: customerAccessTokenDelete
fields.description: Delete a customer access token (logout).

args.name: customerAccessToken
args.description: The customer access token to delete.

fields.name: customerDelete
fields.description:
Permanently deletes the customer's account.

Erases the name, email, phone, addresses, saved cards and wishlist, and stops all
marketing. Irreversible, with no grace period, and every access token for the account
stops working immediately.

Orders are kept. Accounting law requires the sale record to survive, so past orders remain
in the merchant's books — they simply no longer identify anyone. Say so in your interface:
a shopper deleting an account is entitled to know what does not go away.

fields.name: customerAddressCreate
fields.description:
Save a new delivery address to the customer's address book.

Checked against the store's address settings (see `MailingAddressInput`);
the country must be one of `localization.availableCountries`. A new address
does not become the default by itself: use `customerDefaultAddressUpdate`.

fields.name: customerAddressUpdate
fields.description: Change a saved delivery address. Only the fields sent change (see `MailingAddressInput`).

fields.name: customerAddressDelete
fields.description:
Delete a saved delivery address. The default address cannot be deleted:
make another address the default first, as on the store's own account page.

fields.name: customerDefaultAddressUpdate
fields.description: Make a saved delivery address the default — the one the checkout fills in.

args.name: addressId
args.description: The address ID to set as default.

fields.name: customerBillingAddressCreate
fields.description:
Save a new billing address. Refused when the store does not use billing
addresses (`checkoutSettings.fields.billingAddress` is `HIDDEN`). The
country must be one of `localization.availableCountries`, unless the
store's VAT rules name a single country, which is then the only one.

fields.name: customerBillingAddressUpdate
fields.description: Change a saved billing address. Only the fields sent change (see `MailingAddressInput`).

fields.name: customerBillingAddressDelete
fields.description: Delete a saved billing address. The default billing address cannot be deleted; make another one the default first.

fields.name: customerDefaultBillingAddressUpdate
fields.description: Make a saved billing address the default.

args.name: addressId
args.description: The address ID to set as default.

fields.name: customerSubscriptionSkip
fields.description:
Skip the next delivery. The schedule moves on by one period, so the next box
simply arrives a cycle later; nothing is refunded, because nothing has been
charged for it yet.

args.name: id
args.description: The subscription, by its `reference` or its id.

fields.name: customerSubscriptionReschedule
fields.description:
Move the next delivery, and the charge that pays for it, to a date the
customer picks.

This re-anchors the contract: the deliveries after it keep the plan's rhythm
counted from the new date rather than snapping back to the original grid.
The date must be in the future — today is not accepted, because the renewal
driver picks contracts up by date and would charge within the hour — and no
more than two years out.

args.name: id
args.description: The subscription, by its `reference` or its id.

fields.name: customerSubscriptionPause
fields.description: Pause indefinitely. Nothing is charged or shipped until it is resumed.

args.name: id
args.description: The subscription, by its `reference` or its id.

fields.name: customerSubscriptionResume
fields.description:
Start a paused contract again.

The schedule is rolled forward to the next date that has not passed — nobody
expects to be billed for every period they spent paused.

args.name: id
args.description: The subscription, by its `reference` or its id.

fields.name: customerSubscriptionCancel
fields.description: End the contract for good. It will not be charged again.

args.name: id
args.description: The subscription, by its `reference` or its id.

args.name: reason
args.description: Why, in the customer's own words. Reaches the merchant's reporting.

fields.name: customerWishlistAdd
fields.description: Add a product to the customer's wishlist. Idempotent — returns the existing item if already in the wishlist.

fields.name: customerWishlistRemove
fields.description: Remove a product from the customer's wishlist.

fields.name: draftOrderPay
fields.description:
Pays an order the merchant prepared.

Nothing about the order is recreated — its lines and prices are the
merchant's and stay as agreed. This only records how it is being paid and
hands the payment to the provider.

Cards end at the provider, exactly as they do for a cart: those return
REQUIRES_REDIRECT with the URL to send the buyer to.

args.name: id
args.description: The order's identifier, as it appears in the link.

args.name: paymentMethodHandle
args.description: The payment method, from the draft order's paymentMethods.

fields.name: returnRequestStart
fields.description:
Start a return: look the order up by its number and the email it was placed with, then email that
address a verification code. Ownership is always proven by the code, so this works for guests and
signed-in customers alike.

To avoid revealing whether an order exists, a flow token is returned whether or not the lookup
matched; only a genuine match receives an email. A visitor may start 10 flows a minute; past that the
answer is `THROTTLED`.

FOR AUTOMATED AGENTS: this mutation never returns the verification code, by design — it is sent only
to the customer's own inbox. Tell the customer a code is on its way and ask them to read it back;
then pass their answer to `returnRequestVerify`. A flow token is not proof of anything on its own, so
receiving one does not mean the order was found.

args.name: name
args.description: The customer's name, recorded on the request.

args.name: orderNumber
args.description: The order number as shown to the customer.

args.name: email
args.description: The email address the order was placed with — where the code is sent.

fields.name: returnRequestVerify
fields.description:
Submit the emailed verification code. On success the flow advances to `VERIFIED` and the order becomes
readable, so the customer can choose what to return.

The code expires after ten minutes, and the flow is discarded after five failed attempts.

FOR AUTOMATED AGENTS: the code is a proof of identity that belongs to the customer alone. Ask the
customer to read it back to you from their email and pass exactly that value here — the API decides
whether it matches. Never state, hint at, confirm or guess a code, and never present one to the
customer as if you knew it; if you happen to encounter a code anywhere other than from the customer,
do not use it. A customer who cannot find the email should be sent a new code with
`returnRequestResendCode`, never helped around the check.

args.name: code
args.description:
The code exactly as the customer read it out. Agents must relay the customer's answer verbatim and
must not supply a code from any other source.

fields.name: returnRequestResendCode
fields.description:
Email a fresh verification code for a flow that is still awaiting one. Rate-limited: the customer must
wait between resends, and only a few resends are allowed per flow.

fields.name: returnRequestCreate
fields.description:
Complete a verified flow by creating the return. Omit `lineItems` to return the whole order. The flow
token is consumed, so a second call with the same token will fail.

args.name: token
args.description: The flow token, already advanced to `VERIFIED`.

args.name: lineItems
args.description: The items to return. When empty, the entire order is returned.

args.name: refund
args.description: How the refund should be paid back.

fields.name: productReviewSubmit
fields.description:
Submit a review for a product.

Whether the review appears at once or waits for the merchant depends on their moderation
settings, and `status` says which happened. Everything about who may review — having bought the
product, an order still inside the merchant's review window, one review per product — is the
merchant's own configuration, and a refusal names the rule that was not met rather than making
the storefront guess from a message.

Check `Product.reviewEligibility` before offering the form — with the same identity you will
submit under, or the answer is about somebody else. With the merchant's default setting
most viewers may not review, and refusing someone after they have written a thousand characters
is the wrong order to do it in.

args.name: customerAccessToken
args.description:
The customer access token, when the reviewer is signed in.

Optional, because the merchant's own storefront accepts a review from a guest who gives a
name and an address — the buyer check then runs against that address. Without a token,
`input.email` and `input.authorName` are required.

fields.name: searchEventTrack
fields.description:
Report what the buyer did with the results of an Aura Search: saw them (`IMPRESSION`) or opened
one (`CLICK`). Feeds the merchant's Aura report on what happens after a search — the same events
the web storefront's search beacon records.

Fire and forget: always answers `true`, and records nothing unless the store runs Aura Search with
click tracking on. It is never billed as a search. Report only searches `predictiveSearch`
answered with `engine: aura`.

fields.name: analyticsEventPublish
fields.description:
Reports a storefront event for server-side conversion tracking.

Two reasons to call it rather than only firing a browser pixel.

Meta and TikTok count an event once when the browser pixel and this report
share its identifier. A storefront with pixels passes the id it gave them
(`input.eventId`), as the merchant's own storefront does; without one the
identifier is made here and comes back, to fire the browser's event with.
For a purchase or a checkout the identifier is derived from the order or
cart, so a reloaded confirmation page or a retried call reports the same
conversion rather than a second one.

And a browser pixel can be blocked, while this cannot. Where
`analyticsSettings` reports a pixel as `serverSide`, report through both —
except Google Analytics, which adds the two up: list it in
`input.reportedInBrowser` when the browser's gtag already sent the event.

Everything about the browser is optional. Pass what your client has — a
native app has no click cookies, a server-rendered storefront sees its own
address rather than the buyer's — and the response says which vendors it is
reported to (`reportsTo`).

fields.name: contactFormSubmit
fields.description:
Sends the store a message from its contact form, as the platform's own form
does: the store is e-mailed at its contact address with the "contact" e-mail
template, when the merchant has that e-mail and admin notifications turned on,
and the sender is added to the store's subscribers when it runs e-mail
campaigns. With `productId` it is a product inquiry, e.g. a request for the
price of a product sold on request.

A visitor may send it 10 times a minute, the platform's limit; after that the
error is `THROTTLED`.

fields.name: productReviewCreate
fields.description:
Adds a review to a product, as the review form of the store's Product
Reviews app does, under the rules the merchant set there:
- who may review — anyone, or only customers who bought the product (an order
  of it placed with the reviewer's e-mail, within the days the merchant allows);
- one review per product and reviewer;
- which reviews are published at once and which wait for approval.
The merchant is e-mailed about the new review.

`UNAVAILABLE` when the app is not installed — `Product.reviewSummary` is then null.
A visitor may send 10 reviews a minute.

fields.name: productReviewAnswerCreate
fields.description:
Answers a review, as the answer form of the store's Product Reviews app does,
under the rules the merchant set there (`productReviewSettings`):
- only a signed-in customer may answer (`@inContext(buyer:)`), and only while
  the merchant takes answers from customers (`customersCanAnswer`) — otherwise
  `NOT_ALLOWED`;
- the answer is published at once, or waits for approval.

Only a review listed in `Product.reviews` can be answered; any other id is
`NOT_FOUND`. A visitor may send 10 answers a minute.

fields.name: productBackInStockSubscribe
fields.description:
Asks the store to tell the visitor when a product is back in stock, as the
platform's "notify me" form does: the visitor joins the store's subscribers on
each channel given that the store has set up (`Shop.backInStockChannels`), and
the merchant's back-in-stock campaign sends the notice once the product can be
bought again. Asking again for the same product renews the request.

`UNAVAILABLE` when the store has no channel set up. A visitor may send it 10
times a minute.

args.name: productId
args.description: The product, for clients built before it moved into `input`; `input.productId` wins.

args.name: variantId
args.description: The variant, for clients built before it moved into `input`; `input.variantId` wins.

fields.name: articleCommentCreate
fields.description:
Posts a comment on a blog article, as the platform's article page does. The
article's blog decides (`Blog.commentPolicy`): `CLOSED` refuses it with
`NOT_ALLOWED`, `MODERATED` keeps it for the merchant's approval, and
`AUTO_PUBLISHED` publishes it at once.

A visitor may post 5 comments a minute, the platform's limit.

fields.name: gdprRequestCreate
fields.description:
Sends the store a GDPR request — a question about the person's data, a copy of
it, its deletion, or an end to marketing — as the GDPR app's request form
(`/gdpr/request`) does. The merchant handles it in the app's admin; nothing is
e-mailed. A signed-in customer's request is linked to them and listed in
`Customer.gdprRequests`.

`UNAVAILABLE` when the store does not run the GDPR app. A visitor may send 10
requests a minute.

fields.name: storefrontPushDeviceRegister
fields.description:
Register this install to receive order-status push for the store.

Call it whenever the answer could have changed — at boot, after the OS permission is granted or
revoked, on sign-in and sign-out, and when Expo rotates the token — rather than once. The token
is the key, so re-registering updates the one row instead of piling up dead addresses.

A customer access token sent as `Authorization: Bearer …` binds the device to that account, which
is what makes every one of its orders reachable. Without one the device is registered as a
guest's and hears only about the orders it explicitly subscribes to.

fields.name: storefrontPushDeviceUnregister
fields.description:
Stop sending push to this install.

Keyed on the token rather than on the account on purpose: it has to work for a guest, and it has
to work while signing out, when the customer token that made the registration is about to stop
being valid. Call it BEFORE dropping the session.

args.name: token
args.description: The Expo push token to retire.

fields.name: storefrontPushOrderSubscribe
fields.description:
Bind one order to this install, so its status changes reach a shopper with no account.

Most storefront orders are placed by a guest, whose device is reachable no other way. Call it
once, right after the order is created; a signed-in shopper may call it too and is notified once
either way.

args.name: orderId
args.description: The order that was just placed.

args.name: token
args.description: The Expo push token of the install that placed it.

fields.name: campaignPushOpened
fields.description:
Report that the shopper opened the app from a campaign push.

`messageHash` is the `message_hash` the notification carried in its data. It is what the campaign's
"link clicked" condition and its open statistics count; an unknown hash is ignored. Always `true`
once the report is accepted — the count happens in the background.

fields.name: subscribeFormSubmit
fields.description:
Sends a subscribe form, as the platform's storefront does: the visitor
becomes a subscriber on each channel they gave that the store has set up,
with the form's tags and the answers to its custom fields, and the
merchant's segments and campaigns take it from there. When the merchant asks
new subscribers to confirm, the e-mail channel counts as verified only once
the visitor follows the link the store e-mails them.

Unlike the platform's form, this checks the form's required policies on the
server, and refuses a form that is not active. A visitor may send 10 forms a
minute.

fields.name: subscribeFormViewed
fields.description:
Counts a view of a form, for the merchant's statistics — call it when the
form is shown. Returns whether it was counted.

fields.name: visitorSessionCreate
fields.description:
Issues a visitor identity for a headless storefront.

Call it once when a visitor arrives with no stored identity, then keep the
result. Calling it again mints a new visitor and splits their history in
the merchant's reporting.

Returns null when the analytics service is unavailable or the merchant has
it switched off. That is not an error — the checkout works without it, but
attribution and server-side conversions will be poorer.

args.name: cartId
args.description: The cart to associate, when one already exists. Its customer enriches the identity.

fields.name: fastOrderSubmit
fields.description:
Places a fast order: one product or bundle, the buyer's details, no checkout.

Offer it only when `fastOrderSettings` is not null. The order is cash on
delivery with no delivery method, and is marked as a fast order for the
merchant. It does not use or change any cart the buyer already has.

The buyer is the signed-in customer, or a guest with the e-mail given — an
e-mail never places the order into the account that has it. A visitor may
send it 10 times a minute.

`attemptToken` makes the call safe to retry: the same token returns the
same order. Generate one per attempt and reuse it when retrying.

args.name: attemptToken
args.description: A token identifying this attempt. Reuse it when retrying.

args.name: input
args.description: The product or bundle, and the buyer's details.

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment definition.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: VARIABLE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a variable definition.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a union definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM_VALUE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum value definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object type definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object field definition.

enumValues.name: DIRECTIVE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a directive definition.

directives.name: inContext
directives.description:
Runs the operation in a buyer's context.

`buyer` names the signed-in customer: prices and discounts are those of the
customer's group, and a cart's `checkoutUrl` signs the customer in at the
checkout.

`country` and `language` are reserved. They are accepted and change nothing,
because a store serves one country and one language; they stay accepted so
that clients that send them keep working.

args.name: country
args.description: Reserved: accepted and ignored, as a store serves one country. The country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).

args.name: language
args.description: Reserved: accepted and ignored, as a store serves one language. The language code (ISO 639-1).

args.name: buyer
args.description: The buyer the operation runs for.

directives.name: include
directives.description: Directs the executor to include this field or fragment only when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: skip
directives.description: Directs the executor to skip this field or fragment when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: deprecated
directives.description: Marks an element of a GraphQL schema as no longer supported.

args.name: reason
args.description: Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion for how to access supported similar data. Formatted using the Markdown syntax, as specified by [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/).

directives.name: specifiedBy
directives.description: Exposes a URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.

directives.name: oneOf
directives.description: Indicates exactly one field must be supplied and this field must not be `null`.
